11-2B-3. - Standards.
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT11UNDECO_CH2DIRE_ARTBCODI_11-2B-3ST","Title":"11-2B-3. - Standards.","Content":"
\n

\n The standards for all development in the commercial districts shall be as follows:\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Dimensional standards.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Requirements. Table 11-2B-3 of this subsection shall be used for determining required setbacks,\n street and residential landscape buffers and maximum building height standards for\n development in each of the respective commercial districts. Subsections A2 and A3\n of this section and subsection 11-3B-7C1c of this title set forth certain exceptions\n and additional clarification for the dimensional standards.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n TABLE 11-2B-3\n
\n DIMENSIONAL STANDARDS IN THE COMMERCIAL DISTRICTS\n \n

\n
\n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n \n
\n Dimensional Standards\n \n 1, 4\n \n \n C-N\n \n C-C\n \n C-G\n \n L-O\n \n M-E\n \n H-E\n
\n Front setback (in feet)\n \n 0\n
\n Rear setback (in feet)\n \n 0\n
\n Interior side setback (in feet)\n \n 0\n \n 10/5\n \n 2\n \n \n 0\n \n 0\n
\n Street landscape buffer (in feet):\n
\n  Local\n \n 10\n
\n  Collector\n \n 20\n
\n  Arterial\n \n 25\n
\n  Entryway corridor\n \n 35\n
\n  Interstate\n \n 50\n
\n Landscape buffer to residential uses (in feet)\n \n 3\n \n \n 20\n \n 25\n \n 25\n \n 20/10\n \n 2\n \n \n 25\n \n 25\n
\n Maximum building height (in feet)\n \n 35\n \n 50\n \n 65\n \n 35\n \n 65\n \n 95\n
\n Parking requirements\n \n See chapter 3, article C, \"Off Street Parking And Loading Requirements\", of this title\n
\n Landscaping requirements\n \n See chapter 3, article B, \"Landscaping Requirements\", of this title\n
\n
\n

 

\n
\n \n

\n Notes:\n \n

\n \n 1\n \n

\n \t\t\n

\n All setbacks shall be measured from the ultimate right-of-way for the street classification\n as shown on the adopted transportation plan.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n \n 2\n \n

\n \t\t\n

\n Minimum setback only allowed with reuse of existing residential structure.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n \n 3\n \n

\n \t\t\n

\n Where the adjacent property is vacant, the Director shall determine the adjacent property\n designation based on the Comprehensive Plan designation.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n \n 4\n \n

\n \t\t\n

\n Dimensional standards for setbacks, landscape buffers, building heights, and parking\n requirements within adopted specific area plans take precedence over standards provided\n in this table.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Encroachments allowed in any setback. Fire escapes may project a distance not exceeding one (1) foot.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Maximum height limit.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n a.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The maximum height limitations shall not apply to the following architectural features\n not intended for human occupation. steeple, belfry, cupola, chimney. Such architectural\n features shall have a maximum height limit of twenty (20) feet as measured from the\n roofline.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n b.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The maximum height limitations shall not apply to the following: spire; amateur radio\n antenna; bridge tower; fire and hose tower; observation tower; power line tower; smokestack;\n water tank or tower; ventilator; windmill; wireless communication facility, or other\n commercial or personal tower and/or antenna structure; or other appurtenances usually\n required to be placed above the level of the ground and not intended for human occupancy.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n c.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n No exception shall be allowed to the height limit where the height of any structures\n will constitute a hazard to the safe landing and takeoff of aircraft in an established\n airport.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n d.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Additional height not to exceed twenty (20) percent of the maximum height allowed\n for the district may be approved by the Director through the alternative compliance\n procedures set forth in chapter 5, \"administration\", of this title. Additional height\n shall be allowed when the development provides ten (10) percent of the building square\n feet in open space, courtyards, patios, or other usable outdoor space available for\n the employees and/or patrons of the structure, excluding required setbacks and landscape\n buffers.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n e.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Additional height exceeding twenty (20) percent of the maximum height allowed for\n the district or when additional height is requested without providing the required\n open space in accord with subsection (A)(3)d of this section requires approval through\n a conditional use permit.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Hours of operation. Business hours of operation within the L-O and C-N Districts shall be limited from\n 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.. Business hours of operation within the C-C and C-G Districts\n shall be limited from 6:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. when the property abuts a residential\n use or district. Extended hours of operation in the C-C and C-G Districts may be requested\n through a conditional use permit. These restrictions apply to all business operations\n occurring outside an enclosed structure, including, but not limited to, customer or\n client visits, trash compacting, and deliveries. These restrictions do not apply to\n business operations occurring within an enclosed structure, including, but not limited\n to, cleaning, bookkeeping, and after hours work by a limited number of employees.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n (Ord. 05-1170, 8-30-2005, eff. 9-15-2005; Ord. 10-1439, 1-12-2010, eff. 1-18-2010;\n Ord. 14-1623, 9-2-2014; Ord. 19-1833, 7-9-2019)\n
